<Paragraph lead>
Lantern Tiles is a browser puzzle game where you light a dark board one hexagon at a time, before your oil runs out. I played the first two chapters over a weekend. It is quiet, short and clever, with one mistake that spoils the end.
</Paragraph>

## How a level works

Each lantern you place lights the six tiles around it and costs one unit of oil. You start each level with a fixed amount, and the goal is to light every tile.

The board is almost black, and the only colour is the warm light of the lanterns. It looks like a city at night seen from a plane.

<Figure
  src="/src/assets/blog/lantern-tiles-board.png"
  alt="A level halfway through: seven lit lanterns, two mirror tiles and a band of grey fog tiles across the middle"
  caption="Chapter two, level four: mirrors push the light two tiles further."
/>

## Four kinds of tile

The rules stay simple, but each chapter adds a tile that changes how you plan.

- **Plain tiles** light when a lantern touches them.
- **Mirrors** bounce the light two tiles further.
- **Fog** lights only when two lanterns touch it.
- **Wind** blows out a lantern on the edge after three turns.

By the end of chapter two I was planning five moves ahead.

## The harbour level

The best level is The Harbour. The board is shaped like a bay, with water tiles that never light, and you have exactly enough oil if you use every mirror.

I tried it eleven times. When it finally worked, the whole harbour lit up in one sweep and the music came in for the first time.

## Where it falls short

Three things got in the way, and the first one is serious.

| Problem | Where it bites |
| --- | --- |
| Undo goes back one move only | Long levels in chapter three |
| Fog is hard to see on a phone | Any level with fog |
| No keyboard way to move between tiles | Everywhere, if you cannot use a mouse |

The last chapter leans on wind, and one early mistake means starting the level again. I would wait for a longer undo before playing it.

## Verdict

Lantern Tiles is shorter and calmer than other light puzzles I have played. It has about forty levels, a level editor marked as early, and no account or sign-in.

<Callout type="tip" title="My verdict">
Worth an evening if you like slow puzzles where the answer arrives all at once. [Play Lantern Tiles in your browser](/projects/lantern-tiles/).
</Callout>
